experiment: Cooperative token generation and ephemeral chunk metadata preparation
reason: One matched-input trial showed no end-to-end speed improvement; restore the previous four-slot deployment.
candidate: Yield between complete tokenized chunks after a 5 ms cooperative work budget, preserving the shared tokenizer's thread and per-chunk language reset.
Prepare ephemeral chunk metadata in input order without creating a task and timeout wrapper per chunk; yield between chunks.
Record separate search_fields and chunk_metadata stage durations.
validation: Four synthetic search-field tests passed, including interleaved languages and cancellation without background mutation.
Old/new ephemeral metadata equivalence, deterministic IDs, order, source immutability, sanitization and cooperative progress passed.
Six ciphertext/plaintext hashes and per-document chunk counts matched the baseline.
Active text, lexical token, position and chunk-order digests matched for all six documents.
Focused correctness lint and git diff whitespace checks passed. Broad lint retained legacy module warnings; the experimental code was not adopted.
limitations: Single run per condition; the 0.49-second difference does not establish a performance regression or improvement.
Manifest and registration order were unchanged, but concurrent workers reached the single parser in different orders. Individual document times are not controlled paired measurements.
Only the application container was recreated to load the candidate; parser and embedding containers were not restarted.
Cooperative stage durations include time yielded to other tasks; they are not pure CPU compute time.
Groupware checks probe its HTTP entry page, not authenticated business transactions. CPUUsage is an integer sample; reported zero is not proof of zero CPU consumption.
Small HTTP sample counts and other host activity limit causal attribution of the CPU/latency differences.
